summary: Category spend on bid alerts is real, but there is no first-hand evidence that small K-12 MSPs want agenda-stage alerts, Civic IQ already covers this broadly and free, and David has no route to these buyers. Pass unless a hand-built digest first draws interest from real MSP owners.

demand.evidence: Only vendor marketing and a 2015 article; RESEARCH.md found no MSP complaints. The Apify E-rate alert actor has 2 users at $5/mo. BidNet spend proves the category, not this wedge.

statusQuo.evidence: Real workarounds exist (BidNet, Visualping, manual agenda reading, relationships), but they are already paid or cheap and nobody quantifies the hours or deals lost.

specificity.evidence: Owner or sales lead at a 5–50 person K-12 MSP in one state is a filter, not a person; no state chosen and the reach channel is unconfirmed.

wedge.evidence: One state, one trade, a quote-verified weekly email is a good wedge, and a concierge version needs no code. Messy PDFs and BoardDocs make automation noisy.

futureFit.evidence: Cheaper LLM document reading helps incumbents like Civic IQ and BidNet add agenda parsing as easily as it helps a one-person niche product.

premises: Small MSPs miss deals because they learn of purchases at the RFP stage (unsupported)
Agenda-stage signals are early and specific enough to act on (plausible, 6–18 months is a vendor claim)
MSPs will pay $79–$149/mo when BidNet is about $50/mo and Civic IQ is free to start (unsupported)
A free model can classify messy agendas with few false positives (untested)
David can reach these buyers (no evidence)
alternatives: Concierge: hand-build one state's digest for a month and send it to 10 MSPs; no code
Full multi-source engine (Legistar, BoardDocs, Form 470, grants); large effort against funded platforms
Reuse the watch-and-alert pattern from permitly and lienclock for a buyer David can reach
Sell the same signals to school-safety installers or other trades
wedge: One state, 20–50 districts, one weekly email of IT/security signals with a verbatim source quote and link.

feasibility.notes: TypeScript CLI with Vitest on fixtures, free model via LiteLLM. Proving test: a fixture agenda yields exactly one alert whose quote is a substring of the source, stable on re-run. M1 proves extraction only, not demand.

risks: Civic IQ is free to start and BidNet, RFPSchoolWatch and BidPrime are established
No first-hand MSP demand or reach channel
False positives from messy PDFs destroy trust
BoardDocs unsupported by civic-scraper; terms and robots unchecked
Price near or above BidNet in a small niche
killCriteria: Drop if fewer than 3 of 10 contacted MSP owners would pay $79 after a hand-built sample digest, if Civic IQ's free tier already surfaces the same items, if fewer than 8 of 10 sampled alerts check out against the source, or if David cannot name a community to reach MSPs in one state.
